title: ADB Asia SME Monitor 2020: Fintech Loans to Tricycle Drivers (public source)
summary: Asian Development Bank baseline survey of self-employed tricycle drivers in Metro Manila, comparing drivers with IoT-secured fintech vehicle loans and conventional drivers on income, financing, bank accounts and saving.
label_notes: Pages are 1-based PDF page indexes. Fieldwork is 'November-December 2019'; the end of December is used. Drivers were randomly sampled within two groups (conventional drivers in Manila/Quezon City and fintech-loan customers across NCR), so totals describe this sample, not all MSMEs.

findings.text: Only 23% of tricycle drivers had a bank account, below the 2017 Philippine average of 34.5%; drivers with fintech loans had a higher rate (29.5%).
findings.quote: Among tricycle drivers, 23% had bank accounts, well below the Philippine average of 34.5% in 2017

findings.text: Among drivers with a bank account, 60% had a debit card, but only 5% had a credit card and 8% used online or mobile banking.
findings.quote: Among bank account owners, 60% have a debit card, but only 5% have a credit card and 8% use online/mobile banking

findings.text: 44% of drivers said they personally saved or set aside money.
findings.quote: Among drivers, 44% said they personally saved or set aside money

findings.text: 33% of drivers kept savings as cash at home, while only 7% saved in an account at a formal financial institution.
findings.quote: While 33% said they were saving as cash at home, only 7% used an account at a formal financial institution

findings.text: 10% of drivers used informal savings groups such as paluwagan.
findings.quote: with 10% of drivers using informal savings groups

findings.text: Among conventional drivers who own their tricycle, 43.5% financed it through a motorcycle or tricycle dealer and 0.1% through a commercial bank.

subgroup.segment: Conventional drivers who own their tricycle

findings.text: Drivers with fintech loans reported an average daily net salary of P731, against P551 for conventional drivers.
findings.quote: Fintech customers report an average of P731 of daily net salary compared to P551 for conventional customers
